Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0003", "row_sha256": "5e7adea6c390f67bcbfd5c1351e61ccb179e3392edc50ebb006f514627deeffd", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "okay, can you turn this into a proper prompt for the film society’s writing request. the North Quad Film Society is planning a screening of The Glass Orchard on saturday, november 14, 2026, in Alder Hall 204. i need one of two pieces of writing, but which one depends on the licensing update, so please make the condition easy to spot and don’t blend the two outcomes together. the primary thing we want is a public event listing, but only if the campus licensing office has sent written confirmation that we have permission to screen the film by thursday, november 12, at 3:00 p.m. a conversation with someone at the office, or a message saying they expect to send paperwork later, does not count as written confirmation by the deadline.

if that confirmation has arrived by the deadline, ask for a public listing of 120 to 160 words for the society website and campus events calendar. it should be readable by students who have never been to one of our events, not written like an inside joke for the committee. the listing needs to say that the screening is free and open to all currently enrolled students, and that no RSVP is needed. doors open at 6:30 p.m. and the film starts at 7:00 p.m.; put those times in a way that people won’t confuse doors with the start of the film. the room is Alder Hall 204, not the auditorium in Alder Hall, which is a different space and has caused confusion before.

please include the film’s complete title, The Glass Orchard, and identify the host as the North Quad Film Society. the public listing can invite people to stay for a short discussion after the screening, but it must describe that as optional, not part of the film or a requirement for attending. the discussion will be about fifteen minutes and will take place in the same room. no one needs to sign up for it. the society’s committee has not settled on a discussion question, so don’t invent one or suggest that a guest speaker will be there. we don’t have a confirmed guest, and that detail should not appear as a promise or a maybe in the listing.

there are a few practical details that matter more than clever promotional language. use the east entrance of Alder Hall for step-free access to the room; the other entrance has stairs. don’t imply that the east entrance is the only way into the building for everyone, just make the accessible route clear. the screening will have English captions. there is no need to mention food, parking, or a ticket desk because we have not arranged those things and nobody has asked for that information. if it fits naturally, the listing can say that people are welcome to arrive shortly before doors open, but don’t suggest that they can enter the room before 6:30.

if the licensing office has not sent written confirmation by 3:00 p.m. on thursday, november 12, then do not write the public listing, even if the committee is hopeful or the paperwork seems likely. instead, write an internal status note of 80 to 120 words for the North Quad Film Society committee. that is a different useful action, not a second version of the event listing. it should state that the event is planned for saturday, november 14, at 7:00 p.m. in Alder Hall 204, identify the missing written license confirmation as the reason the public listing cannot yet be prepared, and say that doors are currently planned to open at 6:30 p.m. do not claim that the screening is canceled, approved, or definitely going ahead; the committee only needs a clear account of the present status.

for that internal note, mention that the next decision depends on whether written confirmation is received, without making up a new deadline or saying who will contact the office. nobody has assigned that follow-up yet. don’t put the internal note on the society website or frame it as a message to students. it is for committee members who already know the planned event, so it can be direct, but it should still distinguish the current plan from a confirmed license. a spoken assurance does not change the branch: the stated condition is written confirmation from the campus licensing office received by the deadline.

Mina, who is coordinating the calendar entry, said, “Let’s keep the announcement useful for someone deciding whether they can come, rather than making it sound like a private club.” that’s the tone i’m after: welcoming and straightforward, with the event facts easy to scan. don’t turn her comment into another quote in the finished listing, and don’t write a committee discussion of the wording. it is just a guide to the audience and tone. the listing should not claim that the society has screened this film before or explain why the committee selected it, since neither point is part of the information we have.

please keep the public branch focused on the event itself rather than adding a plot summary or a review of The Glass Orchard. we haven’t supplied a synopsis, and guessing what the film is about would be misleading. likewise, don’t add a year, director, runtime, rating, or language for the film; those details are not in the event information. the English captions are a screening access detail, not a reason to infer anything else about the film. keep the supplied title exactly as written, and don’t change the room name or date while making the wording smoother.

in either branch, return only the one piece that matches the condition, with no heading that explains which branch you chose, no prefatory note, and no extra version of the other piece. if written licensing confirmation is in by the deadline, the one output is the public listing within its word range. if it is not in by the deadline, the one output is the internal status note within its word range. the final response should be the requested text itself, not a description of how you made it. the committee also asked that the event time remain clear even if the date is written in a shorter style, and that practical access information not be buried at the end of a long promotional paragraph; those are useful details for readers trying to plan their evening.", "output": "Create one piece of writing for the North Quad Film Society’s planned screening of *The Glass Orchard* on Saturday, November 14, 2026, in Alder Hall 204. Choose the piece solely according to the licensing condition below. Return only the one applicable piece—no branch label, preface, explanation, or second version.

## Licensing condition

The public-listing branch applies only if the campus licensing office has sent written confirmation of permission to screen the film by Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. A conversation with someone at the office or a message saying paperwork is expected later does not count. If written confirmation has not arrived by the deadline, use the internal-note branch, even if approval seems likely.

## If written confirmation arrives by the deadline

Write a 120–160-word public listing for the society website and campus events calendar. Make it welcoming, straightforward, and useful to students unfamiliar with the society. Include:

- The exact film title, *The Glass Orchard*, and the host, North Quad Film Society.
- That the screening is free and open to all currently enrolled students, with no RSVP needed.
- The venue, Alder Hall 204—not the Alder Hall auditorium.
- Doors opening at 6:30 p.m. and the film starting at 7:00 p.m.; make the distinction clear.
- English captions and the east entrance as the step-free route to the room. Do not imply that this is the only entrance for everyone.
- An optional, approximately 15-minute discussion in the same room after the screening. Attendance requires no sign-up. Do not invent a discussion question or suggest a guest speaker.

You may say that people are welcome to arrive shortly before doors open, but do not suggest they can enter the room before 6:30 p.m. Do not add details about food, parking, a ticket desk, a plot, a review, prior screenings, or why the committee chose the film. No synopsis, director, runtime, rating, or film language has been supplied; do not infer these details. Do not include a promise or speculation about a guest.

## If written confirmation has not arrived by the deadline

Do not write a public listing. Instead, write an 80–120-word internal status note for the North Quad Film Society committee. State that the event is planned for Saturday, November 14, at 7:00 p.m. in Alder Hall 204, with doors currently planned to open at 6:30 p.m. Identify the missing written license confirmation as the reason the public listing cannot yet be prepared. Make clear that the next decision depends on whether written confirmation is received, without adding a new deadline or assigning anyone to contact the office. Do not address the note to students or put it on the society website. Do not claim the screening is canceled, approved, or definitely going ahead; distinguish the current plan from a confirmed license.

Use the event time clearly even if you shorten the date, and keep practical access information easy to find rather than burying it at the end of a promotional paragraph. Mina, who is coordinating the calendar entry, said, “Let’s keep the announcement useful for someone deciding whether they can come, rather than making it sound like a private club.” Treat that as tone guidance, not text to quote in the public listing. Return only the applicable requested text."}]
